note: The United Kingdom with its Crown Dependencies, overseas territories, colonies, protectorates and protected states, walked back from 2026.

reviewed.why: The United Kingdom with the Crown Dependencies (Guernsey, Jersey, the Isle of Man), its overseas territories and the Chagos Archipelago, whose land has not changed hands since 1965, and Ireland (the Irish Free State until 1937)

Hong Kong, Brunei, Southern Rhodesia and the colonies in the Caribbean, the Pacific and the Indian Ocean that Britain still held in 1965, with today's borders, until their independence or handover; Weihaiwei, leased from China until 1930

The Gulf protected states, South Arabia with all of Yemen (North Yemen until 1990), and the colonies and protectorates in Africa, the Caribbean, the Pacific and the Indian Ocean that Britain still held in 1965, with today's borders, until their independence

The colonies, protectorates and trust territories Britain held in 1960 in Africa, Asia, the Mediterranean and the Caribbean, with today's borders, until their independence, with Malaya and Somalia around them

The Gold Coast and British Togoland (Ghana), Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and Eritrea, which Britain ruled or ran in the 1950s, with today's borders, and Ethiopia around Eritrea. The Haud, run by Britain inside Ethiopia until 1955, is not drawn

British India (with the princely states, drawn as part of it), Burma and Ceylon, with today's borders, from British rule to today, and Newfoundland until it joined Canada. French and Portuguese India stay with their own families

Mandatory Palestine and Transjordan, and what became of them: Israel, the West Bank, the Gaza Strip, Jordan, and the Sinai occupied by Israel; Iraq, a British mandate until 1932, and Kuwait, occupied by Iraq in 1990-91; Egypt, a British protectorate until 1922 and part of the United Arab Republic in 1958-61

British columns bring the Kachin hills under the rule of British Burma
Britain declares a protectorate over the Shire Highlands, the start of British Central Africa
The states of Sri Menanti accept a British Resident: most of Negeri Sembilan comes under British protection
Emin Pasha leaves Equatoria with Stanley, the last Egyptian province of the Sudan
Pahang accepts a British Resident
Brunei becomes a British protectorate
The Imperial British East Africa Company receives its royal charter
The Fadhli, Lower Aulaqi and Wahidi rulers sign protectorate treaties with Britain
Sarawak becomes a British protectorate
The Qu’aiti and Kathiri sultans of the Hadhramaut accept British protection
The Sultan of the Maldives accepts British protection
British columns occupy the Shan states
Germany extends its New Guinea protectorate to the northern Solomon Islands
The National African Company is chartered as the Royal Niger Company
The Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra signs the first protectorate treaty east of Aden
Lagos is separated from the Gold Coast and becomes a colony of its own
By a treaty with Britain, Johor puts its foreign affairs in British hands
British troops take Mandalay and depose King Thibaw: Upper Burma is annexed on 1 January 1886
Sennar falls to the Mahdists
Kassala falls to the Mahdists after a long siege
The Anglo-Egyptian army leaves Dongola after the failed Gordon relief expedition
Britain declares the Oil Rivers Protectorate on the Niger delta
Britain declares the Bechuanaland Protectorate
A German imperial charter puts the German East Africa Company’s treaty lands under German protection
Khartoum falls to the Mahdi and Gordon is killed
The first British protection treaties are signed with the Somali clans as Egypt leaves the coast
Berber falls to the Mahdists
Lupton Bey surrenders Bahr el Ghazal to the Mahdists
Slatin surrenders Darfur to the Mahdists
El Obeid falls to the Mahdi: Kordofan is lost to Egypt
British troops defeat Urabi at Tel el-Kebir and occupy Egypt
The British North Borneo Company receives its royal charter
Rotuma is ceded to Britain and joins the Colony of Fiji
Britain takes over the administration of Cyprus under the Cyprus Convention; the island stays Ottoman
By the Treaty of Jacobabad the Khan of Kalat accepts British protection; Quetta is leased to Britain
Al-Zubayr Rahma Mansur takes El Fasher: Darfur is annexed to the Egyptian Sudan
Cakobau and the chiefs of Fiji cede the islands to Britain
The Sultan of Selangor accepts a British Resident
Lagos is joined to the new Gold Coast Colony
By the Treaty of Pangkor, Perak accepts a British Resident
Al-Zubayr, master of the Bahr el Ghazal, is made its Egyptian governor
Jassim Al Thani flies the Ottoman flag and lets Ottoman troops into Al Bidda: Qatar becomes an Ottoman district
Cakobau is crowned king of a united Fiji
Samuel Baker proclaims Egyptian rule over Equatoria at Gondokoro
Denmark hands its rights over the Nicobar Islands, abandoned since 1848, to Britain
Moshoeshoe’s Basotho kingdom is taken under British rule as Basutoland
Britain sets up the Naga Hills district, pushing into the hills from Samaguting; Kohima follows in 1878
By the Treaty of Sinchula, after the Duar War, Bhutan cedes the Bengal and Eastern Duars and Kalimpong to Britain
Britain hands the Ionian Islands over to Greece

Bahrain signs a perpetual truce with Britain and comes under its protection
By the Treaty of Tumlong, Sikkim becomes a British protectorate
Britain gives Naya Muluk, the western Terai, back to Nepal for its help in 1857
By the Convention of Peking, China cedes Kowloon, south of today’s Boundary Street, to Britain
By the Treaty of Managua, Britain gives up its protectorate over the Mosquito Coast to Nicaragua
Queen Victoria’s proclamation: the Crown takes over the East India Company’s rule in India
The penal settlement of Port Blair is founded on the Andaman Islands
British troops occupy the island of Perim
The Sultan of Muscat gives the Khuriya Muriya Islands to Britain
After the Second Anglo-Burmese War, Britain annexes the province of Pegu
Britain annexes the Sikkim Terai and the rest of the Darjeeling hills after the Raja of Sikkim had two British travellers seized
After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the East India Company annexes the Punjab
The Sultan of Brunei cedes Labuan to Britain

Charles Napier defeats the Talpur amirs at Miani and Dubba: Sindh is annexed
The Sultan of Brunei makes James Brooke Rajah of Sarawak
Britain annexes the Assam Duars, the foothill passes of Kamrup and Darrang held by Bhutan
British forces take possession of Hong Kong Island
British troops take Aden from the Sultan of Lahej
Pitcairn Island is taken under British protection with its first constitution
After the Coorg War, the East India Company annexes Coorg
Two British warships reassert British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands and the Buenos Aires garrison leaves

The raja of Cachar, driven out by the Burmese, puts his kingdom under British protection
Burmese armies invade Assam for the third time and rule the Ahom kingdom themselves
The sheikhs of the Gulf coast sign the General Maritime Treaty with Britain after the 1819 Ras Al Khaimah campaign
Burma conquers Manipur and holds it for seven years

Britain founds Bathurst (Banjul) on St Mary's Island at the mouth of the Gambia
